messages:
alex: Heads-up — cloud notified a ~12% price cut for H100 in asia-southeast1. Need to re-run commitment / placement models asap.

maria: Wait really? That could change our reserved capacity plan for Q3. Do we have a breakdown by SKU and region? :eyes:

ivan: I pulled a quick delta this morning, rough numbers below. Not final but directional.

ivan: ```
current unit cost (eu-west3 H100): $0.45/hr
current unit cost (asia-southeast1 H100): $0.48/hr
asia new price: -12% => $0.4224/hr
net delta vs eu: ~ -6% (asia now cheaper)
assume 30% of batch traffic shift -> ~540k annual saving (back-of-envelope)
```

sre-jen: Interesting. We must account for egress + latency for EU customers. For sync/low-latency routes, eu affinity still matters. For async batch/optimize workloads, asia shift looks promising.

maria: From pricing/packaging POV: we could either: 1) re-benchmark and lower hosted API price across the board (bad for margin), 2) fold savings into margin and keep prices, 3) introduce region-differentiated price tiers (eu-premium). Thoughts?

finance-bot: Run reservation reopt model? I kicked off a simulation job 1912344700 — result ETA ~2h. Key outputs to look for: incremental cost per reserved GPU, payback period vs on-demand, and revenue-contribution sensitivity by tier.

ops-dan: Also flag compliance: customers with EU data-residency requirements cannot have model state leave region in many contracts. We'll need opt-out or hybrid placements.

alex: Proposal:
- Keep base reserved committed pool in eu for latency/SLA-sensitive customers (50% of current eu reserve)
- Open a new reserved sub-pool in asia for batch/burst workloads (move 30% of batch there)
- Re-run unit-econ: tag sample workloads as sync vs async and compute realized token cost including egress + routing overheads

ivan: Quick calc showing routing/egress impact:
```
assume egress addl cost = $0.02 per request (avg)
if batch payloads large, egress dominates, but for token-only workload egress is small
effective per-token cost shift after egress: -4% vs -6%
```

sre-jen: We'll also need health/availability runbooks for cross-region fallbacks. If asia reserved saturates, automatic fallback to eu must be seamless. Add KV-cache sync considerations.

maria: For customer messaging: I recommend we do not change published prices immediately. Instead:
- Announce improved unit economics to internal teams
- Use savings to fund promotional credits and packaging experiments (e.g., cheaper batch tier)
- Revisit base prices after two quarters of telemetry

finance-bot: Simulation finished. Summary (short):
- Move 30% batch to asia reserved -> gross infra cost down 8%
- Net margin improvement (after egress/ops) -> +3.2% on hosted product P&L
- Break-even on additional reservation rebooking ~ 5 months (given current utilization)

ops-dan: Legal ok with hybrid as long as we give EU customers residency toggle and keep logs/audit in region. Need Product review for UX toggles.

alex: Action items: @ivan re-run the sim with model-level breakdown (gpt-large vs gpt-xl) by EOD. @sre-jen draft fallback runbook. @maria coordinate packaging experiments + messaging. @ops-dan confirm residency flag constraints and any CS/Legal blockers. @finance-bot attach full sim CSV.

maria: One more thought — if we keep prices stable and take margin improvement, we should commit a portion of the gain to infra reliability (reserve margin for preemptible spikes). :+1:

alex: Agree. Let's reconvene after ivan's detailed sim. Thanks all. :rocket

DeployBot: deploy: reservation-sim v2 started by finance-bot (id 0x7f9)
